objects.original: Two normalized exponential tilts of a common base measure and their left-relative-to-right log-density ratio.
objects.reconstructed: The canonical llr of mu.tilted f relative to mu.tilted g, identified with f-log Z_f-g+log Z_g.
objects.evidence: The public theorem and private representative have identical signs and normalizers, while the lesson distinguishes canonical llr from the displayed representative.

domains.original: Normalized common-base tilts, applied to restricted-Gaussian fibers.
domains.reconstructed: An arbitrary measurable space with a sigma-finite common base and integrable exponential weights, including the vacuous zero-base case.
domains.evidence: Restricted-Gaussian fibers are a specialization; the zero left tilt makes the zero-base equality vacuous.

quantifiers.original: For each admissible pair, the identity holds almost everywhere under the left fiber.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every admissible mu, f and g, equality holds mu.tilted f-almost everywhere.
quantifiers.evidence: The proof first establishes a base-a.e. identity and transfers it through tilted absolute continuity without making it pointwise.

assumptions.original: Two admissible normalized exponential tilts of one common base.
assumptions.reconstructed: SigmaFinite mu, Measurable f, Integrable exp(f), and Integrable exp(g), with no separate global Measurable g premise.
assumptions.evidence: These are the declaration's exact hypotheses; integrability supplies the almost-everywhere regularity needed for g.

conclusion.original: The left-relative-to-right log density is the left normalized exponent minus the right normalized exponent.
conclusion.reconstructed: llr(mu.tilted f,mu.tilted g)=f-log Z_f-g+log Z_g under the left tilt.
conclusion.evidence: All terms and signs agree with the normalized quotient and the three llr identities used by Lean.

scopes.original: Representative identification supporting a later score calculation, without a classical-gradient inference.
scopes.reconstructed: Only an a.e. value identity; the separate derivative theorem differentiates an explicit function.
scopes.evidence: Module prose, theorem comments and lesson all retain this boundary.

constant_dependencies.original: Each normalizer depends on its exponent and the common base, not on the evaluation point.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Z_f=integral exp(f) dmu and Z_g=integral exp(g) dmu.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The integration variable is bound and there is no hidden coefficient.

deltas.description: The formal statement exposes the canonical RN representative and the analytic hypotheses implicit in the normalized-density manipulation.
The reusable identity allows general sigma-finite common-base tilts and the vacuous zero-base case beyond the nondegenerate fiber application.

review_evidence: Fresh packet-only review included the exact whole Lean module and authored lesson, checked the private representative, all three proof steps and the final absolute-continuity transfer, and found no blocking mathematical or publication-context delta. A binding-only refresh for the declaration's dedicated Frontier Cell changed no semantic slot or delta.
